notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected because the team requires ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent).
  Before returning any monetary Decimal, check the repo's money module for a rounding helper (e.g. round_money) and wrap the final value with it. Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
- [rb-0003] Handle the empty/zero-denominator case explicitly: The accepted implementation returns ZERO when total quantity is zero, avoiding a division-by-zero for invoices without lines.
  For weighted-average or ratio computations, sum the denominator first and return the module's zero constant when it is zero, rather than relying on the caller or catching exceptions.
- [rb-0004] Match existing error codes and validation style before writing new code: Grep the codebase for BillingError usages and isinstance checks to mirror established conventions rather than inventing new ones.
  Before implementing validation, search sibling modules for existing error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and type-check patterns. Reusing the same codes and message formats keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on error codes.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module and existing helpers before implementing: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py revealed ZERO, to_money, and round_money, which the accepted solution reused instead of raw arithmetic.
  When a task involves amounts, open the money/utility module first and reuse its constants and converters (ZERO, to_money, round_money) so behavior matches the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0005] Guard against bool passing isinstance(x, int): Python's bool is a subclass of int, so quantity validation must explicitly reject booleans.
  When validating an integer parameter, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before range checks; otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0 and corrupt data.
- [rb-0006] Normalize money through the project's helpers before comparing: Convert and round unit_price via to_money/round_money before the negativity check so comparisons use the canonical Decimal form.
  Raw inputs may be strings, ints, or Decimals; passing them through the module's to_money and round_money helpers first ensures the negative check and stored value are consistent and reject floats per existing policy.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating payment state or amounts.
item.content: Scan audit.events(<event_name>) for a matching idempotency_key at the very top of the function; if found, return the original record unchanged. Only after that do state/amount checks, and always include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Apply approval threshold to support-initiated refunds
item.description: Refunds above 500.00 require a second approver; raise BillingError("approval_required") when approved_by is missing.
item.content: Accept keyword-only approved_by=None, compare the rounded amount against a 500.00 threshold, and raise BillingError("approval_required", str(amount)) only when the amount exceeds it and no approver is supplied. Amounts at or below the threshold need no approval.

item.title: Serialize Decimal amounts as float in audit entries
item.description: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal, so audit fields carrying money must be cast with float(amount).
item.content: When calling audit.record for refunds or credits, pass amount=float(amount) and refunded_amount=float(payment.refunded_amount). Keep Decimal arithmetic internally via to_money/round_money; only convert at the audit boundary.
